correctness.rationale: For each d>=3 and R>1, the circular-profile solid T={ (x,z): (||x||-R)^2+z^2<=1 } has boundary S^{d-2}×S^1. Fix a Haar normal with inclination β∈(0,π/2); cross-section coordinates s in meridian line and u=||y||>=0 yield a disk meridian region whose axis contact comprises j=0,1,2 disjoint intervals. Rotational fibers S^{d-3} give j0 type S^{d-3}×D², j1 type D^{d-1}, j2 type S^{d-2}×[0,1], with d3 S^0 causing two disks. For c=R sinβ and t>=0, half-offset lengths (c-1)+, 2 min(c,1), (1-c)+ sum to 1+c; uniform hyperplane inclination density proportional sin^{d-2}β makes X=sinβ, μd=Γ(d/2)^2/[Γ((d-1)/2)Γ((d+1)/2)]. Dividing by Z=1+Rμ gives all three exact probabilities. With N(R)=E min(RX,1), Nprime=E[X 1(X<1/R)] and Ndoubleprime=-f_X(1/R)/R³<0, the numerator of Pballprime strictly decreases from positive at R=1 to negative as R→∞, proving unique global maximizer R_d, bounded R_d<=μd^-2. For Y_d=√d|n_z|=>|Z| with uniform moments and R=1+λ/d, derive d(1-Pball)→F(λ)=E(λ-Z²/2)_+ -λ/2+1/4 uniformly compact; Fprime=2Φ(√(2λ))-3/2 has unique zero λ=q²/2, q=Φ^-1(3/4), and minimum qϕ(q). Compactness of d(R_d-1) and uniqueness give both limits. Independent quadrature/root finding for d=3,4,8,30 reproduces probabilities/optimizers; source check_tube.py inspected. Numerical cases are not the topological or infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: The probability that a random affine hyperplane cuts a natural high-dimensional toroidal solid into a contractible ball is a motivated integral-geometric and topological invariant. The theorem classifies distinct homotopy types for every dimension, determines a unique shape parameter maximizing contractible cuts and gives sharp Gaussian asymptotic loss constants. The d3 formulas alone are known, but the dimensional topology and optimizer are substantive, not a mere parameter substitution.

limitations: The dimension-three Crofton law is known as circular case of a broader convex-meridian result.
Sampling is motion-invariant affine hyperplane measure conditioned on meeting the interior; not central sections or surface-only cuts.
Only first-order optimal d→∞ constants, no uniform error or arbitrary profile theorem.
